name: Request complete
when: A request is marked Done in admin.
subject: Complete: {{request_type}}{{ref}}

vars.first_name: Their first name, blank if we do not have it
vars.request_type: The kind of request, e.g. Text and photos

notes: What they asked for and what we changed are their words and ours, printed as they were written. The two labels above them are editable; the text is not.

name: Quick question about a request
when: A request cannot be started as written, so the bot asks before anyone opens it.
subject: Quick question about your request{{ref}}

slots.lead: Got your request. One thing before we start:
slots.closer: Reply to this email or answer in your portal, whichever is easier, and we'll get on it.

vars.first_name: Their first name, blank if we do not have it

notes: The question itself is written per request and sits in the panel between the lead line and the closer.

name: Portal access invite
when: You invite someone, or a first payment creates the account.
subject: Your WebEaze portal access

slots.lead: You've been given access to the WebEaze portal for {{business}}.
slots.lead_existing: You already have an account, so this link signs you in.
slots.lead_new: Use the link below to set a password and sign in.
slots.expiry: The link expires in 24 hours. If it has, ask for a new invite.

vars.business: Their business name, or 'your business' when we have none on file

notes: One email with two faces: the lead line is followed by 'lead existing' when they already have an account and 'lead new' when they do not, and the button label switches the same way. The business name comes out bold.

name: Sign-in link
when: Someone asks to sign in by email instead of a password.
subject: Your sign-in link

slots.lead: Here's your way in. No password needed.
slots.fine_print: The link works for one hour and only from this email. If you didn't ask for it, you can ignore this: nobody can get in without it.

vars.first_name: Their first name, blank if we do not have it

notes: The inbox preview line and the postal address in the footer stay in the code.

name: Monthly growth report
when: The first of the month, per client.
subject: Your {{month_year}} growth report

slots.opening: Here's a quick update on how {{site}} is doing.
slots.opening_essential: Here's your quick monthly check-in on how {{site}} is doing.
slots.leads_note: Calls, emails, and contact-form messages from your website.
slots.snapshot_intro: Here's a quick snapshot of your site right now:
slots.shipped_intro: Here's what we took care of for you {{month_phrase}}:
slots.recs_intro: A couple of things we'd suggest:
slots.upsell: You're on our Essential plan. Growth adds your search trends over time, the exact terms people use to find you, and a tailored action plan each month.
slots.closing: If you'd like a hand with any of this, send us a request in your

vars.month_year: The month the report covers, with the year, e.g. July 2026. Empty on a report they asked for themselves, and the subject closes up around it
vars.report_period: What the header calls this report: the month name on the monthly run, the word website otherwise
vars.first_name: Their first name, or there if we do not have one
vars.site: Their website address, or the words your website if none is on file
vars.inquiry_word: inquiry or inquiries, matching the count beside it
vars.leads_label: When those inquiries came in, e.g. in July or this month
vars.month_phrase: in July on the monthly run, this month on an on-demand send
vars.month_label: Just the month name, e.g. July. Empty on an on-demand send
vars.leads_count: How many inquiries came in, the big number in the callout

notes: Only the sentences are editable. The speed, rating and search lines, the AI summary, the recommendations, the list of work completed and the address footer all stay in code. Closing runs straight into the client portal link, so it deliberately ends without a full stop.

name: New inquiry from your site
when: Someone fills in a form on their website.
subject: New inquiry: {{who}}{{phone_suffix}}

slots.intro: Hi {{first_name}}, a new inquiry just came in
slots.headline: {{who}} wants to hear from you
slots.dropped_note: Couldn't attach: {{dropped}}. Ask them to email it to you directly.
slots.footer: Replying quickly is the single biggest thing that wins this job. Everything is also in your

vars.first_name: The client's first name, or there if we do not have one
vars.who: The visitor's name, or Someone if they did not give one
vars.who_short: The visitor's name for the call button, or them if they did not give one
vars.phone_suffix: The visitor's phone in brackets for the subject, e.g. (302-555-0101), or nothing
vars.dropped: The files we could not attach, comma separated

notes: A form that sets its own subject still overrides the subject line. The submitted details, the Phone, Email and Page labels and the visitor's own field names are printed as they came in and are not editable. Footer runs straight into the portal link, so it deliberately ends without a full stop.

name: Daily lead summary
when: Once a day, if anyone got in touch.
subject: Your website got {{lead_count}} {{lead_word}} today

slots.headline_one: You got a new lead today{{lead_summary}}.
slots.nudge_contactable: The faster you follow up, the more likely you are to win the job.
slots.nudge_anonymous: Nothing to reply to on this one, but it's a sign your site is doing its job.
slots.nudge_basic: Open your portal to see them and follow up.
slots.spam_note_one: {{skipped_count}} suspected sales pitch left out of this email. It's still in your portal if you want to look.
slots.spam_note_many: {{skipped_count}} suspected sales pitches left out of this email. They're still in your portal if you want to look.
slots.footer: This is your daily lead summary from WebEaze. Every lead is also in {{portal_link}} in real time. To stop these daily emails, open {{leads_link}} and switch off the daily summary.

vars.lead_word: lead or leads, to match the count
vars.lead_summary: The breakdown after the count, e.g. ": 2 form submissions and a phone call"
vars.more_count: How many leads did not fit in the email
vars.skipped_count: How many suspected pitches were left out
vars.portal_link: Where the portal link goes in the footer
vars.leads_link: Where the Leads page link goes in the footer

notes: Each lead card (the Name, Phone, Email and Message rows, the Call and Reply buttons, and the line about people who only tapped your number) is built per lead and is not editable.

name: How is your website working
when: A while after launch, once.
subject: How is your website working out?

slots.lead: Your website has been live for a couple of weeks now. How's it going? We hope it's already bringing you new leads and customers.
slots.asks_intro: Two quick things, only if you're happy so far:
slots.review_ask: A quick {{review_link}} genuinely means a lot to a small team like ours.
slots.referral_ask: Know another business owner who needs a site? {{referral_link}} and you get a free month when they sign up.
slots.closer: And if you'd like any changes, just send us a request in your {{portal_link}}. That's what we're here for.

vars.first_name: Their first name, "there" if we do not have it
vars.review_link: Where the Google review link goes
vars.referral_link: Where the referrals page link goes

notes: The three link addresses are fixed in code; the words around them, and the link text itself, are yours. Move a link placeholder and the link moves with it.

name: Your portal is waiting
when: They have never opened their portal.
subject: Your WebEaze portal is waiting

slots.lead: We set your client portal up when you joined, but it looks like you haven't opened it yet. Everything we do for you lives in there.
slots.list_items:
Send us website changes and watch them get done
See who has been contacting you through your site
Check how your site is performing on Google
slots.closer: If you can't get in, or never received your login, just reply to this email and we'll sort it out.

vars.first_name: Their first name, "there" if we do not have it

notes: List items is one bullet per line, so a bullet can be added or removed here.

name: Waiting on you
when: A request has been waiting on their reply for three days.
subject: Still waiting on you: {{request_type}}

slots.lead: We're still waiting to hear back on your {{request_type_lower}} request. It's paused until we do.
slots.closer: You can also just reply to this email and we'll pick it up from there.

vars.first_name: Their first name, "there" if we do not have it
vars.request_type: The kind of request as it is written, e.g. Text and photos
vars.request_type_lower: The same thing in lower case, for mid sentence

notes: The question we asked is quoted underneath the label in the words it was asked in; that panel is not editable.

name: We'd love you back
when: A couple of weeks after a plan ends, before the files are deleted.
subject: We'd love to have you back at WebEaze

slots.lead: It has been a couple of weeks since your plan with us ended, and we wanted to reach out once more before your website files are removed.
slots.offer: If you'd like to come back, we can reactivate your site and pick up right where we left off, no rebuild needed.
slots.policy: Please note: after 30 days from cancellation, website files are permanently deleted and there are no extensions/exceptions to this policy.
slots.closer: Either way, thank you for having been part of us, and we wish you the best in your future endeavors.

vars.first_name: Their first name, "there" if we do not have it

notes: The 30 day deletion window is our policy, not a date this email works out.

name: Finish your site setup
when: Setup has not been submitted yet.
subject: Let's get your website started

slots.lead: Welcome again! We noticed your Site Setup isn't finished yet. We can't start building your website until we have a few details about your business, so you're happy with the final result.
slots.nudge: It only takes a few minutes. The sooner you complete it, the sooner your site goes live.
slots.closer: If you have questions or need help getting started, reply to this email and we'll help you out.

vars.first_name: Their first name, "there" if we do not have it

name: Inquiries still waiting
when: Inquiries from their site have sat unmarked for a week.
subject: {{inquiry_count}} {{inquiry_word}} {{is_are}} still waiting for you

slots.lead: {{inquiry_count}} {{inquiry_word}} came in through your website and we have not heard how {{it}} went.
slots.follow_up: Already spoken to {{them}}? Tap below and we will stop mentioning {{it}}. If not, most people ring two or three businesses and go with whoever answers first, so today is worth more than tomorrow.
slots.closer: One tap is all it takes, no login. We send this at most once a week, and never twice about the same inquiry.

vars.first_name: Their first name, "there" if we do not have it
vars.inquiry_count: How many inquiries, or the word An when there is only one
vars.inquiry_word: inquiry or inquiries, the spelling the body happens to use
vars.is_are: is or are, to match the count
vars.isnt_arent: isn't or aren't, to match the count
vars.them: them for one inquiry, them all for several
vars.it: it for one inquiry, them for several
vars.more_count: How many inquiries did not fit in the list

notes: This email has always said inquiry in the subject and inquiry in the body. Both are editable now, so they can be made to agree. The list itself is built per inquiry and is not editable.

name: Confirm your new address
when: They change the email on their account.
subject: Confirm your new WebEaze email address

slots.lead: You asked to sign in to your WebEaze portal with this address instead of {{old_email}}. Confirm it and we will move it across.
slots.fine_print: The link works for one hour. Until you use it, nothing changes and you keep signing in with your old address.

vars.old_email: The address they sign in with today
vars.new_email: The address they asked to move to

notes: This is the confirmation sent to the NEW address only. The two other messages this sends, the heads-up to the old address and the 'your email is updated' note, are still in code.

name: Reward unlocked
when: A referral or milestone earns them something.
subject: You unlocked a reward!

slots.reward_heading: A little something for sticking with us
slots.reward_lead: Thanks for being such a loyal WebEaze client. You just unlocked a reward:
slots.reward_closer: There's nothing you need to do. We'll apply it and send a note to your account in the portal once it's done.
slots.reward_portal_line: You can see your notes and milestones any time in your
slots.milestone_more: Keep going and there are three rewards waiting further along, at 25, 50 and 100 completed requests. You can see how close you are in your portal.

vars.first_name: Their first name. The greeting line is skipped entirely when we do not have one
vars.milestone: The milestone just reached, e.g. 5 requests completed
vars.reward: The perk unlocked, e.g. A free month, on us (reward variant only)

notes: One key, two versions of the same moment: the reward slots are for a milestone that carries a perk, the milestone slots for one that does not. A key holds one subject, so the subject field is the reward version and milestone subject is the plain one. The milestone's own name, its blurb, the reward wording and the address footer stay in code.

name: Conversations waiting on us
when: Clients are waiting on a reply from us.
subject: Waiting on you: {{waiting_count}} {{reply_word}}

slots.lead: {{waiting_count}} {{conversation_word}} {{is_are}} waiting on a reply from us, oldest first.

vars.waiting_count: How many conversations are waiting on us
vars.reply_word: reply or replies, to match the count
vars.conversation_word: conversation or conversations, to match the count
vars.is_are: is or are, to match the count
vars.days: How many days that one conversation has been waiting
vars.day_word: day or days, to match that number

notes: Yours, not a client's, and deliberately separate from the client chase that shares the phrase. Each row is built per conversation; only the waiting line is wording.

name: Site watch alert
when: A client site goes down or breaks a check.
subject: Site watch: {{count}} new {{issue_word}} to look at

slots.closer: Mark each fixed in the admin once handled, and the client will see it as "recently handled".

vars.count: How many new issues this run found
vars.issue_word: issue or issues, to match the count

notes: The list of what broke (client, kind, detail) is the findings, not copy, and stays in code.

name: Churn digest
when: Weekly, for accounts going quiet.
subject: {{count}} {{client_word}} to check on this week

slots.heading: Reach out before they leave
slots.lead: {{count}} active {{client_word}} showing churn signals this week, ranked by risk. Activity is based on their last request, leads, open issues, and renewal date.
slots.footnote: You are getting this because these accounts crossed the churn-risk threshold. A quiet week means no email.

vars.count: How many at-risk clients are in this digest
vars.client_word: client or clients, to match the count

notes: The ranked table, the risk dots and the reason on each row are what the scoring found, so they stay in code.

name: Add-on invoice drafted
when: A client orders a flat-rate add-on.
subject: Invoice {{state}}: {{addon}} for {{client_name}}

slots.status_sent: Stripe has emailed it to them and they can pay from the portal too. You get another email the moment it is paid, and the work files itself as a request. Nothing for you to send.
slots.status_finalized: It is finalized and they have a Pay now link in the portal, but Stripe did not email it. Worth sending from the dashboard.
slots.status_draft: It is sitting in Stripe as a draft. Review it and hit Send.
slots.mismatch: the portal showed ${{shown}} but the invoice is ${{invoiced}}. Worth lining those up.

vars.state: sent, or ready (not emailed) when Stripe would not send it
vars.client_name: Their name, or their email, or a client when we have neither
vars.shown: The price the portal card showed them, in dollars
vars.invoiced: The price the invoice actually came to, in dollars

notes: Exactly one of the three status lines prints, picked by what Stripe did. The client and add-on names, the price, their brief and the note about where the price came from are the facts of that one invoice and stay in code.

name: Card declined
when: The moment Stripe reports a failed payment.
subject: Your card didn't go through

slots.lead: Your card was declined when we tried to take this month's payment. It happens all the time, usually an expired card or a bank being careful, and it takes a minute to sort.
slots.reassure: Nothing has changed with your website and nothing is at risk today. We'll try the card again over the next few days.
slots.closer: If the card is fine and you think this is a mistake, just reply to this email and we'll look into it with you.

vars.first_name: Their first name, "there" if we do not have it

name: Card declined, day three
when: Three days into a run of failed payments, if the card still has not been fixed.
subject: Still no luck with your card

slots.lead: We've tried your card a few times since Tuesday and it's still being declined, so this month's payment hasn't gone through.
slots.ask: Updating the card takes about a minute and puts everything straight away. Your site, your email and your updates all carry on as normal once it goes through.
slots.closer: If something has changed on your end, or now isn't a good time, reply and tell us. We'd far rather work it out with you than have this run on.

vars.first_name: Their first name, "there" if we do not have it

name: Card declined, day seven
when: A week in. The last email before a subscription lapses.
subject: Your website is at risk

slots.lead: It's been a week and your card is still being declined, so this month's payment is outstanding.
slots.warn: We have to be straight with you about what happens next: once a subscription lapses, the hosting it pays for goes with it, and that takes the website offline. We don't want that and we won't do it without talking to you first.
slots.closer: If money is tight right now, say so. We've sorted out payment plans with people before and we'd rather do that than lose you over a bad month.

vars.first_name: Their first name, "there" if we do not have it

name: Payment sorted
when: A payment goes through after we chased them. Not sent if they were never chased.
subject: That's sorted, thank you

slots.lead: Your payment went through, so that's all sorted. Nothing more for you to do, and thank you for getting it sorted quickly.

vars.first_name: Their first name, "there" if we do not have it
